subject: Competitive bake-off recap — PulseHealth / Redwood Inference
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@pulsehealth.com>; Priya Desai <priya.desai@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap — PulseHealth / Redwood Inference

Alex / Priya — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the bake-off discussion so we’re all aligned and so Marissa / Rishi know the ask.

Key pain points you called out:
- Latency spikes in current assistant during peak hours (p95 often > 800ms) causing degraded UX.
- Token cost on high-volume triage workflows is eating into margin (~$0.07 per end-user interaction).
- Need for predictable performance for compliance and on-call SLAs (esp. after Q3 launch).

Goals for the bake-off / evaluation window:
1) Validate an endpoint with p95 latency <= 300ms for typical triage prompts (seq len ~150).
2) Demonstrate at-scale throughput of ~400 concurrent requests with steady latency and <5% error rate.
3) Show a path to ~30–40% per-token cost reductions through batching + caching/quant recommendations.
4) Confirm security posture: SOC2 evidence + ability to run in your VPC for PH-regulated data.

Competitive landscape (what you told us you’re comparing):
- Redwood Inference (us): focus on unified runtime + routing/fallbacks, autoscaling, dedicated capacity options.
- Vendor B: strong fine-tuning options but unclear predictable latency at scale.
- Vendor C: cheaper per-token list price but no private VPC deployment.

Open questions we committed to answer / next steps:
- Marissa: send bake-off scorecard and test plan (attached).
- Rishi: provide estimated committed pricing for a dedicated pool and burst policy.
- Aditya: schedule throughput/latency test window (you suggested next Tue/Wed) and confirm telemetry hooks (traces/tags) we’ll surface.
- Alex/Priya: confirm which real prompts/annotated test data you want us to run, and whether we can use a subset of production traffic (anonymized).

Attachments included: bakeoff-scorecard.xlsx (scorecard + criteria), PulseHealth_RFP_responses.pdf (security + compliance answers).

If that looks right, we’ll schedule the 2-hour test window for next Tuesday morning PT and lock in the test criteria.

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

[Attachment: bakeoff-scorecard.xlsx]
[Attachment: PulseHealth_RFP_responses.pdf]

From: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@pulsehealth.com>

Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@pulsehealth.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap — PulseHealth / Redwood Inference

Thanks Aditya — good summary. A couple clarifications and adds from our side: 

Decision criteria (ranked):
1) Consistent p95 latency under your stated load (this is make-or-break).
2) Security & VPC/on-prem options (we need >= SOC2 + ability to host in our VPC).
3) Cost per active user over a 6-month projection.
4) Ease of rollout and developer ergonomics (SDKs, feature flags, routing controls).

Open questions / requests:
- Can Redwood provide an A/A run against our baseline and then a short A/B to compare quality/perf? We’d like to avoid confounding differences in prompt engineering.
- For the perf test, we’ll provide ~1,500 anonymized sample prompts in a CSV — Marissa, can you ingest those?
- Security: need Clarke (infosec) to see the SOC2 + data flows. Can you add an architecture diagram with network flow?

Timing: Tue/Wed next week works. We prefer Wed 9–11am PT for the test window.

Thanks — Alex

--
Alex Taylor
Head of AI Product — PulseHealth
alex.taylor@pulsehealth.com | (617) 555-0114

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@pulsehealth.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap — Competitive bake-off scorecard + proposed test plan

Alex / Priya — looping back with the proposed test plan and what we’ll deliver during the Wed 9–11am PT window. High-level plan below; full details are in the attached scorecard + test scripts.

Proposed test plan (Wed 9–11am PT):
- 9:00–9:15am: Quick kickoff, verify telemetry and tagging (trace ids + request ids).
- 9:15–9:45am: A/A baseline run using your anonymized prompts against your current provider (you’ll run) and Redwood (we’ll run) with identical prompt templates.
- 9:45–10:30am: A/B quality + perf run (randomized), under increasing concurrency to reach ~400 concurrent connections. We’ll record p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rates, and token consumption.
- 10:30–10:50am: Security check-in with Clarke (infosec) and quick review of network flow diagram.
- 10:50–11:00am: Debrief and immediate next steps (data exports, logs, follow-up items).

Acceptance criteria we’ll score in the bakeoff-scorecard.xlsx: latency thresholds, error rate, token cost per request, functional correctness (automated heuristics + human spot-check), and infra operational aspects (failover, autoscaling behavior).

Follow-up items we’ll action before Wed:
- Rishi: send committed pricing for a 6-month dedicated pool with optional burst capacity (cc’d).
- Aditya: confirm we can get the anonymized CSV ingested and that we’ll have telemetry endpoints configured.
- Alex: send Clarke’s contact and the SOC2 reviewer access (we’ll share a private read-only link to our security artifacts).

Attachments: bakeoff-scorecard.xlsx (detailed rubric and scoring sheet), redwood-performance-metrics.png (sample traces from similar customers).

If that plan looks good I’ll add the calendar invite and include Zoom + perf load generator details.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0147

Thanks Marissa — plan looks solid. I’ve looped Clarke (infosec) on a separate thread and shared the anonymized CSV to the Drive folder you listed. Quick confirmations: 

- Wed 9–11am PT confirmed (we’ll expect the Zoom link + load generator config in the invite).
- We’ll run the A/A baseline on our side at 9:15 and share results.
- Clarke will review SOC2 + architecture diagram; we expect feedback by EOD Wed.

One last ask — for the cost projection, can Rishi include a simple 6-month cost model (tokens/month, reserved pool cost, and expected savings with batching)? That’ll help our finance team compare apples-to-apples.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the test.

Alex
